key_insight: HERMES shifts LCU operator processing to classical computation, estimating transformed-state expectation values from reusable measurements of the original quantum state.
engineering_relevance: It eliminates ancillas, controlled unitaries, and quantum implementation of the transformation operator, reducing hardware demands on NISQ and early fault-tolerant devices.
method: Expand the transformation operator and observable in the Pauli basis, then sample Pauli-term pairs classically.
Compute the target expectation as a ratio of weighted sums of Pauli measurements on the unmodified state.
Deduplicate Pauli terms and group commuting measurements to bound distinct measurement settings independently of classical sample count.
evidence_signal: In H₂ and LiH imaginary-time ground-state energy evaluations, HERMES matched or outperformed a Pauli single-ancilla LCU baseline, showed greater noise robustness, and completed a noisy LiH simulation infeasible for that baseline.
watch_item: Classical overhead grows with the number of Pauli terms in the transformation operator; bounded measurement settings do not imply bounded total measurement shots.
paper_title: Hardware-Friendly Estimation of LCU-Based Expectation Values via Quantum-to-Classical Workload Shifting
